title: Affle 3I Ltd - 542752 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Affle 3i Q4 FY26 revenue rose 20.3% y-o-y to INR 7.24 billion; FY26 revenue INR 27.1 billion (+19.5%) and EBITDA margin 22.5%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue of INR 7.24 billion grew 20.3% y-o-y and 1% q-o-q, marking a 13th consecutive quarter of sequential growth despite geopolitical softness. EBITDA was INR 1.61 billion (22.3% margin, broadly flat y-o-y margin), and PAT was INR 1.20 billion (+16% y-o-y), held back by a low tax base in Q4 FY25. For FY26, revenue was INR 27.1 billion, EBITDA INR 6.10 billion (+26.3%) and PAT INR 4.55 billion (+19.1%). Management said inventory and data costs are rising as a deliberate investment in premium, verticalized inventory, and a roughly one-year investment phase is expected before margins improve. The board approved a preferential warrant issue to Affle Holdings (~INR 11 billion, 25% upfront) to fund acquisitions expected to be concluded within the calendar year.

+16.0% y-o-y, +0.2% q-o-q; subdued by low Q4 FY25 tax rate

segments.name: CPCU business (Q4 FY26)
segments.commentary: 120.3 million conversions at a CPCU rate of INR 60.0, generating CPCU revenue of INR 7.21 billion.

segments.name: India + emerging markets (Q4 FY26)
segments.commentary: Contributed 71.6% of revenue and grew 21.2% y-o-y; on an adjusted basis India grew 19.5% and Emerging Markets 22.3% y-o-y.

segments.name: Developed markets (Q4 FY26)
segments.commentary: Contributed 28.4% of revenue, growing 18.0% y-o-y; management describes this region as under-calibrated and a focus for investment.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term guidance of 20% revenue CAGR reaffirmed; management says organic growth modelled at about 20% and a 10x decadal revenue vision is 'on track'.
Combined entity (post-acquisition) targeted to average around 20% growth with EBITDA margin of about 23% to 25% over time.
Inventory and data costs expected to stay range-bound within the unit economic model; investment phase expected to last about one more year, after which margins should improve progressively.
Management says it will take an acquisition of a meaningful size within the calendar year 2026; may do more than one transaction through FY27.
Modelling 2% long-term average inflation in planning.
capex_capacity: Preferential issue: Affle Holdings to acquire ~7.4 million warrants at INR 1,487 each, totalling ~INR 11 billion, with 25% paid upfront, subject to shareholder approval.
Management says the company already holds substantial cash; the warrant route was chosen to show certainty of funds during deal negotiations.

Around 10 companies evaluated and about 4 shortlisted for deeper due diligence; target profile is a company with a direct advertiser base, sales team and existing integrations in developed markets (North America, Europe).
Past acquisitions (2020-2023) were loss-making or breakeven and have been converted to the CPCU model; management expects a 1-3 year conversion timeline for any new target.
Borrowings being repaid; cash balance accumulating per management.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 was affected by geopolitical softness in select markets and verticals; Jan-Mar is seasonally weaker with no festive quarter benefit.
Management says ~75% of revenue goes direct to advertisers; 25%+ comes through large ad agency group partners, with direct integration to the advertiser app still required.
Management argues the competitive edge is direct advertiser integration, verticalization and CPCU model; sees no significant change in competitor landscape.
CPCU pricing has risen over the last 10 years per management; premium, high lifetime value targeting (premium devices, CTV, premium placements) is the stated reason for higher inventory costs.
Management declined to share repeat-customer percentages or names; says engagement is cyclical, typically budget-to-budget.
Q4 inventory and data costs were 63.3% of revenue, up ~90 bps q-o-q; gross margin has declined over the last 7-8 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross margin declining for the last 7-8 quarters, and is it competition, mix or conscious investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a conscious investment in verticalization, premium inventory, CTV and first-party data integration, mainly in developed markets. Management expects roughly one year more of investment before benefits and a return toward better margin levels.

qa_highlights.question: Ticket size and asset focus for M&A (reference ~USD 200 million)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a size; deals range from small to larger. It said the company is ready to execute in the short term but will be patient on price and terms.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for an acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a meaningfully sized transaction is realistically possible within the calendar year, with no firm timeline until definitive agreements are near.

qa_highlights.question: Is 20% organic growth too conservative given AI tailwinds, and how does 10x fit with inorganic growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 20% organic is a calibrated plan, not base effect. Faster growth would bring lower-quality revenue; the company declines some orders it judges unprofitable. Management expects the combined entity to average around 20% growth with 23-25% EBITDA margins over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why a warrant route rather than QIP, and what is Affle Holdings' funding source?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash is already substantial and the warrants provide certainty of funds during negotiations. It said it is an Affle 3i matter and any Affle Holdings funding notification would be disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Other expenses fell ~3% in FY26 and other income fell ~17%; why?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the other-expense decline mainly to lower business promotion spend, which is concentrated in Q1-Q3. Other income declined from treasury, with exchange gains and lower cash from debt repayment.

risks_watch: Gross margin compression from data and inventory investment; watch whether the one-year investment phase delivers a margin recovery.
Timing and size of acquisitions in calendar 2026, plus integration risk for loss-making targets converted to CPCU.
Demand softness from geopolitical events and any recession-driven pullback in advertiser budgets.
Preferential warrant issue (INR 11 billion, 25% upfront) pending shareholder approval; watch the balance of the 75% remaining payment and Affle Holdings' funding source.
Exchange-rate volatility affecting other income and costs for data and offshore employees.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on long-term growth, AI and the CPCU model, but cautious on the near term, acknowledging a tough Jan-Mar 2026 quarter. Management was evasive on customer-level detail (repeat customers, acquisition size, Affle Holdings' funding) and deferred those to later disclosure.
key_quotes: We are firmly on course to deliver on our medium-term guidance of 20% CAGR as we progress towards our 10x decadal growth vision.
This area of investment has been a conscious decision.
There's a realistic chance that we may conclude a meaningfully sized transaction within this year itself.
We were able to grow at least the top line better and maybe even EBITDA better than the last quarter.

growth.why: Management reaffirmed about 20% organic revenue CAGR over the next 5 years and a 23-25% combined EBITDA margin over time, but no specific capacity, orders or contracts were quantified; backing is mainly demand, CPCU pricing and an acquisition plan with no concrete timing for revenue contribution.
